title: Routing DSL reconciler and validator playbook (incremental migration)
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Goal: introduce a reconciler that validates routing DSL configs against a versioned canonical schema and provides safe, incremental migration paths.

Problem statement:
- Current routing rules are expressed in multiple DSL variants and ad-hoc JSON configs; validation logic is scattered across the policy gateway, sidecar, and the backfill scripts.
- This causes silent incompatibilities when new region/tier/fallback fields are introduced, leading to misrouted requests or mismatched model-variant fallbacks under load.

Deliverables:
1) A standalone schema reconciler service (read-only for now) that ingests a policy bundle and emits a validation report + suggested fixes.
2) A staged migration playbook to convert existing rule sets to schema v2 with automated autofixes where safe.
3) A runtime-compatible validator library (mini-API) to be embedded in the policy engine and console linting.
4) Comprehensive test harness: unit tests, fuzz tests, and a dataset of real-world routing configs (anonymized) for regression checks.

Non-goals:
- Replacing the entire policy interpreter in this sprint. We focus on validation and migration guidance only.

Success metrics:
- 95% of sampled configs pass schema v2 validation with zero manual edits after automated fixes.
- No increase in routing misroutes observed in canary traffic (tracked on canary-routes dashboard).
- Validator runs in <50ms median when invoked as part of the preflight pipeline.

Trade-offs / decisions to make:
- How aggressive should autofix be? (conservative by default; opt-in autofix flag).
- Schema strictness vs backward compatibility: support a compatibility mode for legacy tenants.
- Where to host reconciler: integrated into console backend vs separate microservice.

Plan / milestones:
- Week 1: Design doc + schema v2 draft (done).
- Week 2: Implement core reconciler + canonicalizer prototype (branch: feat/reconciler-proto).
- Week 3: Build validator library + console linter hook.
- Week 4: Fuzzing + safe autofix rules + migration runner.
- Week 5: Canary rollout with opt-in projects and monitoring.

Risks:
- Incorrect autofix could silently change routing semantics for high-impact tenants. Mitigation: require opt-in and human approval for any autofix that changes region/tier semantics.
- Performance regression when validator invoked inline. Mitigation: cache last-successful-validated-hash and fast-path for unchanged bundles.
